root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `zend_std_get_property_ptr_ptr()` continues past `zend_deprecated_dynamic_property(...)`, the object-store slot for `zobj->handle` must still be valid; if the user error handler destroyed `zobj`, the function must stop instead of reaching the later `zobj->properties` read.
root_cause_criterion.description: On the vulnerable path, `zend_deprecated_dynamic_property(zobj->ce, name)` enters `zend_error()` without pinning or revalidating `zobj`. The user error handler can drop the last reference, `zend_objects_store_del()` invalidates the slot and frees the object, and control still returns to the caller. The fixed program pins `zobj` in the helper and bails out when the callback destroys it, so the same post-callback point either sees a still-valid slot or does not reach the protected read.

nodes.state: After the deprecation callback returns, `zend_std_get_property_ptr_ptr()` immediately evaluates `zobj->properties`; on the crashing path this is the ASan-reported read from the same stale `zobj` pointer.

`zend_objects_store_del()` invalidates `EG(objects_store).object_buckets[handle]`, runs the object's `free_obj`, and `efree()`s the tracked `zend_object`; any raw `zobj` pointer still held by the caller becomes dangling.

edges.relation: The same `zobj` pointer that returns from `zend_deprecated_dynamic_property()` is the pointer immediately dereferenced by the later `zobj->properties` read.
The `zend_object *object` deleted by the user-error-handler cleanup is the same `zobj` later read at the sink, establishing the free-before-use on one object.
